Hi Emma — thanks for the thoughtful questions and great to meet today. High level answers below; forwarding to our security lead Nikhil for technical confirmation and retention details. I've also attached our data retention summary and a short SOC2 summary you can share with legal.

- Storage of prompts/outputs: Hosted (default) — prompts and model outputs may be logged and retained to support billing, abuse/safety analysis, and model quality monitoring. For hosted customers we retain these artifacts by default for 30 days.
- Disable logging: For Dedicated and Private deployments we offer options to disable persistent logging entirely (zero retention) or to keep only aggregated telemetry. For Hosted customers, we can discuss contractual options (DPA addendum) and enterprise settings that minimize retention.
- Encryption: All persisted data and logs are encrypted in transit and at rest (TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest). Access is restricted via role-based controls and audit logging.
- Data residency: We support region restrictions — you can pin your tenant to a single region (us-east-1) on Hosted Enterprise, or choose Dedicated/Private installations for stricter residency guarantees.
- PII redaction: We provide server-side SDK hooks and recommended client-side pre-processing. We also offer optional redaction tooling (PII scrubbers) and integration patterns we can share. For highest assurance, we recommend client-side scrubbing + Dedicated/Private deployment.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf (summary), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level).

Next steps: 1) I can schedule a 30-min call with Nikhil to walk through retention and contractual options; 2) If you can share the security checklist from FinSecure, we’ll respond point-by-point.

Hi Emma — quick technical follow-up from Security. Adding concrete retention figures and recommended controls below. Happy to review on a call.

Retention & storage (hosted):
- Default: prompts + outputs retained for 30 days (used for billing, safety review, model quality).
- Optional longer retention: up to 90 days can be enabled for account-level analytics if requested and contractually approved.

Dedicated/Private:
- Retention fully configurable by the customer; can be set to 0 days (no persistent storage of prompts/outputs) and only aggregated telemetry retained.

Storage & encryption:
- Persisted artifacts are stored in customer-scoped S3 buckets (hosted: managed SaaS buckets, dedicated/private: customer-managed or dedicated buckets). Data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Access controls: strict RBAC, KMS-managed keys (customer KMS for Dedicated/Private). Audit logs for admin access are retained per contract (default 90 days for admin audit events).

Logging & caches:
- Short-lived caches (KV cache) are in-memory on GPU hosts and not persisted beyond instance lifecycle unless explicitly checkpointed.
- Operational logs (indexing for debugging) are rotated and indexed only for 7 days by default; those can be shortened per account.

PII mitigation recommendations:
1) Client-side scrubbing: remove/replace direct identifiers before sending requests.
2) Prompt templating: use placeholders for sensitive fields and supply values at runtime where possible.
3) Use Dedicated/Private deployment for regulated workloads requiring strict residency and zero-retention guarantees.

Contractual items we can provide: DPA (data processing addendum), subprocessor list, SOC2 report, and a short security checklist tailored for procurement. For deletion upon contract termination: we support documented data deletion (including S3 object deletion and key rotation) with export of customer-owned artifacts; include this in the SOW/DPA.

Link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/security/soc2-summary (redacted copy).

If helpful, we can produce a 1-page checklist and a short timeline for data deletion post-termination (typically 30 days to fully purge managed buckets unless otherwise specified in the SOW).

Regards,
